old_public_statement:
Refuted statement: "for an arbitrary smooth equation of state $p=p(\epsilon)$
with $\epsilon+p>0$ (no sign restriction on $p'$), the Einstein-fluid system
has a local development depending continuously on the data in a fixed Sobolev
topology."
proposed_public_statement:
Refuted statement: "At every constant rest state with $H_0=\epsilon_0+p(\epsilon_0)>0$, the fixed-flat-background linearized barotropic fluid equations admit a periodic $C^1$ solution on some positive time interval for every smooth periodic initial datum, and their solution operators are continuous in each fixed integer Sobolev topology $H^r$, $r\ge0$, at every fixed positive time."

For $p'(\epsilon_0)=-a^2<0$, both assertions fail: the explicit smooth datum of step 2.2 has no such solution on any positive time interval, and the smooth single-mode sequence of step 2.1 proves failure of $H^r$ continuity for every integer $r\ge0$ at every fixed positive time. These conclusions concern the specified linearized equations; nonlinear Einstein-fluid illposedness with constrained data remains an open prerequisite.
old_page_paragraph:
**Failure without sound-speed positivity.**
[[cex-gr-negative-sound-speed-derivative-breaks-evolution]] linearizes the
barotropic system at a state with $p'(\epsilon_0)<0$, exhibits the Fourier
modes growing like $\cosh(\sqrt{-p'}n t)$ and shows that no fixed-Sobolev
local existence with continuous dependence can hold without a positivity
hypothesis on $p'$.
proposed_page_paragraph:
**Failure without sound-speed positivity in the linearized fluid.**
[[cex-gr-negative-sound-speed-derivative-breaks-evolution]] linearizes the fixed-flat-background barotropic equations at a rest state with $p'(\epsilon_0)<0$. Its explicit smooth Fourier datum has no periodic classical linearized solution on any positive interval, and its smooth single-mode sequence defeats continuity in every fixed integer Sobolev topology at each positive time. A nonlinear Einstein-fluid result must additionally control the constrained initial data and nonlinear evolution; that transfer remains an open prerequisite.
